body: This seems to be related to https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/6145. In both cases, changing the first character of the tag from lowercase to uppercase results in missing properties that the valid-jsdoc rule is expecting. Changing the characters back to lowercase fixes the issue. I'm unsure if capitalized tag names are valid JSDoc or not. If we don't want to allow capitalized tag names, then the fix is in valid-jsdoc itself and should be pretty straightforward (should warn when it comes across a capitalized name). If do want to allow capitalized tag names, I think the change might have to happen in Doctrine itself.

**What version of ESLint are you using?**

**What did you do? Please include the actual source code causing the issue.**

Code causing the error:

``` js
    /**
     * Performs API command 
     *
     * @param {Object} parameters
     * @param {Object} parameters.reportID 
     * @Param {Object} parameters.bankAccountID from.
     * @return {APIDeferred}

```

**What did you expect to happen?**
I expected the linter to pass, but kept getting this error that didn't indicate what the issue might be.

After some deduction, I was able to determine that the root case was `@Param` as opposed to `@param`

issue.title: Support case insensitive tags
issue.body:
**What version are you using?**
master

**What JSDoc comment were you trying to parse?**
/*\* @Const {String} constname */

**What Doctrine options were you using (sloppy, unwrap, etc.)?**
{ unwrap: true }

**What happened? Include output if possible.**
Tag gets parsed as 

```
{ description: '{String} constname', title: 'Const' }
```

**What did you expect to happen?**
Tag gets parsed as 

```
{
  description: null,
  name: 'constname',
  title: 'Const',
  type: { name: 'String', type: 'NameExpression' }
}
```

See eslint related issues: https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/6121 https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/6145
